title: おどるポンポコリン (Odoru Ponpokorin — Dancing Ponpokorin)
description:
The iconic ending theme of 'ちびまる子ちゃん' (Chibi Maruko-chan), the beloved slice-of-life anime about a dreamy third-grade girl in 1970s Shizuoka. Written by the manga's creator さくらももこ (Sakura Momoko) and composed by 織田哲郎 (Oda Tetsurō), the song shot to #1 on the Oricon charts in 1990 and sold over 2.7 million copies — one of the best-selling Japanese singles of all time. It is one of the most universally recognised songs in Japan and remains a karaoke staple across all generations.

The nonsense-word title 'ポンポコリン' and the cheerful 'ピーヒャラ' refrain make it instantly memorable even for new learners. The lyrics are deliberately playful and absurdist — a parade of dancing characters interrupted by random 'facts' like 'Edison was a great man' and 'Kiosks are inside train stations', all delivered with cheerful confidence.

For learners: Excellent N4 listening material. Key vocabulary: おどる (to dance), 登場 (entrance, appearance), いつだって (always), わすれない (won't forget), えらい人 (great person), 常識 (common sense / common knowledge), 有名 (famous), 迷わない (won't hesitate). The 'ピーヒャラ' sections give learners a break while reinforcing the melody, and the two nearly-identical verses make it easy to follow along from the second run.
